source: ACIAR Monograph No. 146a, "ដំណាំសំណែកសៀង" [Soybean Growers Manual], Belfield S., Brown C., Martin M. (eds.), New South Wales Department of Primary Industries / Murdoch University / CARDI / ACIAR, 2012
text: A full chapter covers soybean plant morphology to help farmers recognize growth stages and diagnose problems: seed structure (hilum, seed coat, epicotyl, hypocotyl, cotyledons, radicle) illustrated with a labeled seed diagram; root system structure including the taproot and lateral roots that host the nitrogen-fixing nodules (Bradyrhizobium spp.) which the manual illustrates with a root photo showing visible nodules; stem and leaf structure including trifoliate leaf arrangement, xylem/phloem function in nutrient and water transport, and leaf area's role in yield (leaf area index concepts); and flower/pod/seed development, noting flowers are borne in racemes in leaf axils and that a single plant produces many flowers, only a fraction of which set pods that reach maturity.
